subject.title: [Bug]: MidTurnPrecheckSignal leaks error to UI via pushLoopFailure before internal retry completes

question: Should the durable fix keep this control-flow handling inside the embedded runner boundary, or introduce a generic agent-core bubble-control contract for selected errors?
rationale: The source-level bug is clear, but the open fix candidate was blocked because hard-coding OpenClaw's sentinel in reusable agent-core may be the wrong owner boundary.

options.title: Embedded-runner-owned recovery
options.body: Keep agent-core generic and catch or prevent the signal inside the embedded runner so successful recovery never emits a failure event.

options.title: Generic agent-core seam
options.body: Add an explicit package-level contract that lets callers declare selected errors as non-failure control flow, with agent-core tests for settled-event behavior.

options.title: Accept the current PR shape
options.body: Allow the existing candidate PR's sentinel matching after proof and tests, trading a faster fix for a less clean package boundary.

recommendation.title: Embedded-runner-owned recovery
recommendation.body: Keep agent-core generic and catch or prevent the signal inside the embedded runner so successful recovery never emits a failure event.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle is tied to the original mid-turn precheck path and the current open candidate PR that already explores the boundary fix.
